target.title: fix: strip conda env marker from host tool runs
target.body:
Closes #99424

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OpenClaw from an activated Conda environment could have OpenClaw-managed host tool subprocesses inherit `CONDA_PREFIX`. That active-environment marker can redirect Python package managers or nested tools into the parent environment even though the tool command itself does not show that coupling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing host exec env sanitizer already strips `VIRTUAL_ENV` from inherited and requested override env, but the same policy did not include `CONDA_PREFIX`. This change adds `CONDA_PREFIX` to the shared host env security policy, regenerates the macOS policy mirror, and extends the sanitizer/baseline tests so both inherited env and request-scoped overrides are covered.

This is intentionally limited to `CONDA_PREFIX`; it does not change `PATH` handling or add broad Conda-specific environment filtering.

## User Impact

Users can launch OpenClaw from a Conda-activated shell without that active environment marker leaking into OpenClaw-managed host subprocesses. Existing trusted inherited environment behavior remains unchanged except for this single marker.

## Evidence

- Before/source proof on current main:

  ```shell
  PS> git show origin/main:src/infra/host-env-security-policy.json | Select-String -Pattern 'VIRTUAL_ENV|CONDA_PREFIX'

      "VIRTUAL_ENV",
  ```

  `VIRTUAL_ENV` was covered, while `CONDA_PREFIX` was absent from the policy.

- After this patch:
  - `CONDA_PREFIX` is present in `src/infra/host-env-security-policy.json`.
  - `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/HostEnvSecurityPolicy.generated.swift` is regenerated from the shared policy.
  - `src/infra/host-env-security.test.ts` asserts inherited `CONDA_PREFIX` is stripped and requested `CONDA_PREFIX` overrides are rejected.
  - `src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.test.ts` keeps the reported baseline count aligned.

- After-fix terminal proof from a Conda-activated shell on Windows:

  ```text
  PS> D:\anaconda\Scripts\conda.exe run -n base cmd.exe /d /c "pnpm exec tsx ...\conda-host-env-proof.ts"
  parent_CONDA_PREFIX=<set>
  sanitized_env_has_CONDA_PREFIX=false
  override_rejected_CONDA_PREFIX=true
  child_CONDA_PREFIX=<unset>
  child_OPENCLAW_CLI=1
  child_exit_status=0
  ```

  The probe runs in Conda `base`, exercises OpenClaw's host exec sanitizer from this PR branch, and launches a child process with the sanitized OpenClaw-managed env. The parent has `CONDA_PREFIX`; the OpenClaw-launched child does not.

- Commands run:
  - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/host-env-security.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.policy-parity.test.ts` → 42 tests passed
  - `node scripts/generate-host-env-security-policy-swift.mjs --check` → OK
  - `pnpm exec oxlint src/infra/host-env-security.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.policy-parity.test.ts` → clean
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/infra/host-env-security-policy.json src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.json src/infra/host-env-security.reported-baseline.test.ts src/infra/host-env-security.test.ts apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/HostEnvSecurityPolicy.generated.swift` → clean
  - `git diff --check` → clean
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` → `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`

What was not tested: a full interactive OpenClaw agent turn from Conda was not run. The terminal proof uses a real Conda-activated shell and the same OpenClaw host exec sanitizer boundary that manages inherited and requested env for OpenClaw-launched subprocesses.
